environment.directories: lab: http://198.18.0.1:8080/; realworld and startup: http://213.163.75.157:56050/ (temporary, on p2p-relay1); relay step: 127.0.0.1 on the Hetzner machine
environment.paths: As in campaign 1. Lab: every access link 10 ms each way, relay link 10 ms each way (direct RTT ~40 ms, relayed ~80 ms); lossy1 50 ms + 1 % loss each way. Hetzner <-> i3D host: per flow either ~34 ms or ~37.5 ms RTT (both campaigns show the two clusters, e.g. relay-only runs alternate between them; probably ECMP routing by port); lab nodes with uplink=real reach the real relay through the i3D host's hairpin NAT in < 1 ms.
environment.bench_settings: defaults of 3fb1e9c: latency 10 s at 200 ms, 64 B; upload and download 10 MB each, stopped at 8 s (an upload is reset there and the listener reports what arrived; the bench waits at most 3 s more for that count); concurrency 8 streams of 256 KiB echo requests, 8 MB, requests still running at 8 s are cut off (unfinished, not failures); relay transfers capped at 4 MB; timeout 10 s; --compare-relay and --idle 60s where listed. The relay group uses --relay-only on both sides; the parallel relay runs skip the concurrency phase.
environment.method: Same scenarios, run counts and order as campaign 1 (harness/campaign/campaign2.sh): every run starts fresh processes (new iroh keys and ports; bench uses a temporary identity); 3 runs per scenario, rounds interleaved; parallel relay runs: 2 rounds of 2 and of 4 benches. Scenario side a = the bench (client, dialer), b = the listen node. Verdicts classified by summarize.py, which judges each campaign by the rules of its bench (packet_loss: 2 % of the whole connection in campaign 1, 0.5 % of >= 50 latency-phase packets now); re-run on campaign 1's raw data it reproduces campaign 1's classification exactly.
environment.sides: a = the node running `golem-p2p bench` (it dials), b = the node running `golem-p2p listen`

observations.title: Outcomes unchanged, and the two lost connections are gone
observations.detail: Every scenario has the same direct/relay outcome as in campaign 1; on lab-netem-pr the 2 runs whose connection was closed now end direct (final paths of the 93 peer runs: 51 direct, 42 relay, 0 failed; campaign 1: 49/42/2). RTT, throughput, bind and connect times match campaign 1 within noise in the lab; real-world differences come from the two internet route clusters (~34 / ~37.5 ms) between the i3D host and Hetzner.

observations.title: Verdicts: 88 runs right, 23 misleading, 0 wrong (campaign 1: 81 / 28 / 2)
observations.detail: Every misleading and wrong class of campaign 1 is gone: symmetric NAT now named (hard_nat_likely, 9 runs), Hetzner relay-only verdicts name the peer or a firewall in front of this machine instead of 'two NATs' (6), packet_loss no longer fires on congestion (6), the wrong QAD port is named as a possible cause (6), and the lossy link no longer says 'through a relay' for a closed direct connection. The 23 remaining misleading runs are new: 21 packet_loss false positives (20 clean lab runs with hole punching, 1 real-world), 2 relay_fallback_failed on the lossy link (one of them also misses the 1 % loss).

observations.title: The latency-phase packet_loss hint fires on clean links whenever hole punching finishes during the latency phase
observations.detail: In the lab, 20 of the 21 clean-link runs that started on the relay and went direct ~70-90 ms into the latency phase counted 1-6 of ~120 latency-phase packets as lost, and all 20 got the hint, while all 12 runs that were direct from the first packet and all 12 relay-only runs counted 0 (table.md, latency loss column). debug/latency-loss (noq trace, pr2 -> pr1, 3 of 127 lost): all 3 losses happen within 75 ms after the connect phase, on path 0 (the relay path). iroh's NAT-traversal PATH_CHALLENGEs to the peer's candidate addresses and the off-path PATH_RESPONSEs use path 0's packet numbers; those dropped by the peer's NAT filter before the hole is open (or sent to its private address) are declared lost (lost_bytes 0), and a relayed packet (PATH_NEW_CONNECTION_ID, 56 bytes, RTT 80 ms) was declared lost when the ACK for a later probe sent directly (RTT 40 ms) arrived first (packet-reordering threshold). Neither is loss on the link. One lost packet is enough for the hint (0.5 % of ~120). Possible fixes: start the latency phase's loss count once the path is settled (after the first direct path plus one RTT, or skip the first second), use the selected path's own counters, or require more than one loss event.

observations.title: A lost connection after request timeouts no longer happens on the lossy link
observations.detail: lab-netem-pr: 0 of 3 connections closed (campaign 1: 2 of 3, final_path unknown, QUIC counters lost, verdict 'through a relay'); final path direct and peer.quic present in every run, connection_lost null, duration 61-69 s. The bench itself no longer times requests out there: the concurrency phase now cuts off requests at --transfer-time (8 s, 24 unfinished, 0 failed), before the 10 s request timeout. The per-request timeout was exercised on the listener side: in run 3 its 10 s receive limit timed out the 8 cut-off requests, and the connection carried on (relay comparison and the end of the run followed on it). No run in the campaign lost a connection.

observations.title: relay_fallback_failed on a slow relay path that works
observations.detail: lab-netem-pr runs 1 and 3: 'The relay-only connection to the peer did not work ... If hole punching fails, this peer cannot be reached', exit 5, although the relay connection answered 24-25 latency requests and downloaded at 0.6-1.2 Mbps. The relayed upload was stopped at 8 s; the bench waits 3 s for the listener's count, but the stream reset reached the listener about 5 s after the stop (5.3 s in run 1, 4.9 s in run 3, from the phase timestamps and the listener's 'request sink relay' event, followed by 'peer rejected the stream' because the bench had given up), queued behind seconds of upload data on the relay path (15-21 % of the relayed QUIC packets lost). In campaign 1 the bench waited for the count without a limit, and it arrived 3.7-6.1 s after the 8 s mark (relayed uploads of 11.7-14.1 s, 1.2-2.3 Mbps), so 3 s is too short for such a path. Waiting longer for the count on a relay path, or reporting a timed-out count as 'upload throughput unknown' instead of a failed relay connection, would fix the verdict.

observations.title: Concurrency gives no number on slow links
observations.detail: lab-netem-pr: on ~1-2 Mbps all 8 parallel 256 KiB requests are still running at 8 s in every run, so concurrency is ok with throughput null (campaign 1 measured 2.4 Mbps in one run, the other two failed). Counting the bytes of unfinished requests, or smaller requests on slow paths, would keep the measurement.

observations.title: Wrong QAD port: the message now names both causes
observations.detail: startup-*-qad-7842: udp_blocked 'Either outgoing UDP is blocked on your network ..., or the relay does not serve address discovery on port 7842: if it uses another port, add ,quic=PORT to --relay' (quic_port_explicit false). With the port given explicitly (lab relay ,quic=7842, real relay ,quic=56001) UDP-blocked nodes get 'outgoing UDP is probably blocked' (9 runs). The local-only headline still reads 'Problems found on your network' and exits 5 in the wrong-port case.

observations.title: Runs on the lossy link are shorter but still dominated by relay_compare
observations.detail: lab-netem-pr: 61-69 s (campaign 1: 68-81 s); upload <= 8.1 s (was up to 17.3 s), download and concurrency 8.0 s each, relay_compare 28-33 s (5 s latency, connect, a relayed upload of 8 s + up to 3 s and a download of 8 s, then closing). Clean runs are unchanged (12.6-20.4 s, 72.7 s with --idle 60s).

observations.title: rw-easy-to-open starts on the relay now
observations.detail: Direct 3/3 as before, but first path relay and direct after ~148 ms instead of direct from the first packet: this time the lab node's direct flows to Hetzner took the ~37 ms route and the relayed path was 34.5 ms, so the relay answered the handshake first (campaign 1: 33.7 ms direct vs 34.4 ms relay). Throughput of these direct flows is ~8 % lower (134 vs 146 Mbps, slow start at the higher RTT). Environment, not a code change; the same route split shows in relay-single (67.6 ms now, 74.5 ms then).

observations.title: The real relay is not a bottleneck at the tested load (unchanged)
observations.detail: Relay-only Hetzner -> p2p-relay1 -> Hetzner: 39-43 Mbps per 4 MB transfer alone, with 2 and with 4 at once (~158 Mbps aggregate), no packets dropped by the relay; 418.4 MB through the relay in total, as in campaign 1.

limitations: 3 runs per scenario (4-8 for the parallel relay runs): percentiles over runs are rough; RTT percentiles pool the ~50 latency samples of each run. The lossy-link medians in particular (1.1-30 Mbps per run) say little.

The verdict classification is ours (summarize.py), per run by its worst finding; a 'right' run can still have imperfect wording. A packet_loss hint on an unshaped path counts as misleading, also in the real world where one lost packet may be real.

The lab NATs are Linux conntrack + nftables with port preservation, one host per router, silent drops of unsolicited packets and one mapping timeout; the 'inbound packet steals the port' behaviour of the i3D host's NAT is not reproduced, and a NAT reboot keeps the same ports.
One relay per scenario: mapping_varies_by_dest cannot be measured, so hard_nat (two relays) was never exercised; hard_nat_likely (one relay, port not preserved) was.
No rate limits in the lab and fixed transfer sizes (10 MB direct, 4 MB relayed): throughput numbers show slow start for those sizes, not capacity.
Real world: one location (Helsinki) and one firewall type (ufw); per-flow routes of ~34 or ~37.5 ms between the i3D host and Hetzner shift RTT and throughput by ~8 % between runs and campaigns.

The bench-side request timeout was not exercised (concurrency requests are cut off at 8 s, before the 10 s timeout); connection survival after a timeout was seen on the listener side only (8 timeouts in one run).
The relay load test is bounded (at most 4 parallel 4 MB transfers, ~150 MB through the relay) and does not find the relay's capacity.
--idle cannot show NAT mapping expiry: iroh keeps every path alive every 5 s and the lab's shortest mapping timeout is 5 s.
QUIC loss is counted only for packets the bench node sent; IPv4 only inside the lab.
Runs were sequential, but the i3D host also carries other services; their load was not controlled.

comparison.title: Same outcomes, no failures.
comparison.detail: All 35 scenarios keep their direct/relay outcome; final paths 51 direct / 42 relay / 0 failed (campaign 1: 49 / 42 / 2 failed, the two lossy-link runs whose connection was closed). Lab RTT, throughput, bind and connect times are unchanged within noise; real-world RTT/throughput moved by the two internet route clusters (~34 / ~37.5 ms), not by the code.

comparison.title: Verdict accuracy: 88 right / 23 misleading / 0 wrong runs (was 81 / 28 / 2).
comparison.detail: Fixed: symmetric NAT named via hard_nat_likely (9 runs), no 'two NATs' for the NAT-less Hetzner side (6), no packet_loss on congestion (6), wrong QAD port named as a possible cause (6), no 'through a relay' for a lost direct connection (2 wrong). New: packet_loss false positives in 21 runs (20 clean lab runs whose hole punching finished during the latency phase, 1 real-world) and relay_fallback_failed on the lossy link's slow but working relay path (2).

comparison.title: Lossy link (lab-netem-pr):
comparison.detail: connection survives 3/3 (was closed in 2/3), final path direct and QUIC counters present in every run; runs 61-69 s (was 68-81 s); packet_loss hint in 2/3 (was 0/3); but the concurrency phase yields no throughput (all requests cut off at 8 s) and 2/3 runs report relay_fallback_failed because the relayed upload's count arrives later than the 3 s the bench waits.

comparison.title: Connection survival after timeouts:
comparison.detail: 0 connections lost in 93 peer runs (was 2). The bench no longer times requests out on the lossy link (cut off at 8 s instead); the listener timed out 8 requests in one run without closing the connection.

comparison.title: Regressions:
comparison.detail: (1) packet_loss false positives from hole-punching probes and reordering counted as latency-phase loss (debug/latency-loss); (2) relay_fallback_failed on a slow relay path; (3) no concurrency throughput on slow links. No measurement regressions; rw-easy-to-open's relay-first start and lower RTT/throughput are routing.
